definitions.explanation: The organized relocation of people or assets away from areas of danger, especially during wartime. Most commonly associated with the mass evacuation of urban residents to the countryside during World War II.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちは{田舎|いなか}に{疎開|そかい}した。
examples.english: The children were evacuated to the countryside.

examples.japanese: {戦争中|せんそうちゅう}、{多|おお}くの{学校|がっこう}が{集団|しゅうだん}{疎開|そかい}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: During the war, many schools carried out group evacuations.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{戦時中|せんじちゅう}の{疎開|そかい}{先|さき}での{生活|せいかつ}について、よく{話|はなし}をしてくれた。
examples.english: My grandmother often told me about her life at the place where she was evacuated during the war.

notes:
HISTORICAL CONTEXT:
During World War II, as Japanese cities came under air raids, the government organized mass evacuations ({疎開|そかい}) of civilians, especially children, to rural areas. {学童疎開|がくどうそかい} (schoolchild evacuation) is one of the most well-known aspects of wartime Japan, frequently depicted in literature and film.

Also functions as a する verb: {疎開|そかい}する (to evacuate, to be evacuated).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {避難|ひなん}: evacuation/taking refuge — broader term used for any emergency
- {疎開|そかい}: specifically wartime dispersal of population or assets

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {疎開|そかい}する: to evacuate
- {疎開|そかい}{先|さき}: evacuation destination
- {集団|しゅうだん}{疎開|そかい}: group evacuation
- {学童|がくどう}{疎開|そかい}: schoolchild evacuation
